la:noun:Volcanus.html:
Volcānus (less correctly Vulc-), i, m.
Lit., Vulcan, the fire-god, son of Jupiter and Juno, ; ; ; ; ; ; .—Hence,
Vol-cānĭus (Vulc-), a, um, adj., of or relating to Vulcan, Vulcanian: vis, i. e. fire, Lucil. ap. ; so, acies,a conflagration,; and pestis,: arma,; cf.: munera, currus,: Lemnos,sacred to Vulcan,: insulae,.—
Volcānālis (Vulc-), e, adj., of or belonging to Vulcan: flamen, Müll.—As subst.: Vol-cānālĭa, ium, n. (sc. festa), the yearly festival of Vulcan, celebrated on the 23d of August, Müll.; ; ; ap. ; ; .—
Transf., fire: Volcanum in cornu conclusum gerere,: totis Volcanum spargere tectis,; ; .

la:other:Volcae.gloss: A Gallic tribal confederation of Gallia Narbonensis whose chief towns were Nemausus and Tolosa.

la:other:Volcae.html:
Volcae, ārum, m.,
a numerous and powerful people in Gallia Narbonensis, divided into the Volcae Arecomici and the Volcae Tectosages, ; ; ; ; the former had for their chief town Nemausus, the modern Nismes; the latter, Tolosa, the modern Toulouse, ; .
